newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cuts oil spill estimate to 1,550 kl.
newsitem.headline: Japan cuts oil spill estimate to 1,550 kl.

text.p: Japanese officials said on Thursday they had sharply reduced the estimate of the amount of crude oil that spilled from a supertanker into Tokyo Bay to 1,550 kilolitres, or about one-tenth of the original estimate.
Transport Minister Makoto Koga told a news conference the government had revised the size of the leak to 1,550 kilolitres or 1,315 tonnes. That would be equivalent to 9,800 barrels.
On Wednesday, officials had estimated that 13,400 tonnes (100,000 barrels) had leaked from the supertanker Diamond Grace after it hit a reef in shallow waters of Tokyo Bay.
That would have made it Japan's largest ever oil spill.
The government quickly mobilised a fleet of some 330 ships to tackle the spill and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto declared the situation an emergency.

Asked about the estimated size of the spill, a spokesman for the coastguard or Maritime Safety Agency told Reuters: "We don't know why there was such a huge discrepancy. But anyway it's better than what we had last night."
